items.title: INFLUENCE OF PROBLEMATIC SMARTPHONE AND SOCIAL MEDIA USE ON MUSCULOSKELETAL HEALTH: FROM CHRONIC DISORDERS TO ACUTE INJURIES
items.abstract: Smartphones and social media platforms are integral to communication, education, employment, entertainment, and social interaction. Although research on problematic smartphone and social media use has focused mainly on psychological and behavioral outcomes, increasing evidence indicates relevant physical and musculoskeletal consequences. This narrative review synthesizes evidence concerning chronic musculoskeletal symptoms, postural and biomechanical factors, myofascial findings, and acute injuries associated with smartphone use, and considers behavioral injury pathways related to social media. Relevant systematic reviews, meta-analyses, observational studies, experimental investigations, emergency-department surveillance studies, and scholarly syntheses were identified through targeted literature searches and reference tracing. Intensive or problematic smartphone use is associated with symptoms involving the neck, upper back, shoulders, wrists, hands, and thumbs, although causal relationships remain uncertain. Acute-injury studies document sprains, strains, fractures, hand and wrist trauma, head and neck injuries, falls, and transportation-related injuries associated with mobile-device involvement. Pediatric studies and experimental pedestrian research support distraction as an important mechanism. Emerging evidence also documents physical harm associated with risky social-media challenges and social-media-related interpersonal violence. Smartphone- and social-media-related physical health risks therefore extend beyond chronic postural complaints and involve mechanical, attentional, environmental, and behavioral mechanisms. Prevention should combine ergonomic education, movement variability, distraction awareness, digital-health literacy, age-specific injury prevention, and responsible engagement with social-media content.

items.abstract: This article aims to examine the impacts of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on contemporary legal practice. It begins with a historical overview of AI's emergence and its development to the present day, highlighting the technological advances that have reshaped the legal profession. Through a bibliographic review—especially based on the works of Cláudio Canuto and Thiago Massicano—the research analyzes the implementation of AI-based tools in law firms, their contributions to procedural efficiency, and the ethical and legal challenges they raise. In conclusion, the article projects the future of the legal profession, reflecting on the limits of replacing human performance with technological evolution.

items.title: Job Satisfaction Organizational Commitment and Employee Performance
items.abstract: Job satisfaction and organizational commitment are associated with employee performance, yet these relationships do not explain how favorable attitudes become effective contributions. This article develops a conceptual model of that transition through an integrative reading of research on work attitudes, meaningful work, social exchange, motivation, and work design. The model proposes that employees interpret satisfying work experiences in relation to organizational purposes, develop affective commitment, form intentions to reciprocate valued treatment, and direct available resources toward specific work activities. Organizational justice is proposed to condition selected attitudinal transitions, while the design of digital work may facilitate or obstruct the conversion of resource allocation into performance. The synthesis identifies three central problems in existing explanations: insufficient separation of adjacent constructs, limited evidence for temporal ordering, and the treatment of resources as available without examining their deployment. Eight propositions address these problems while retaining direct, reverse, and competing explanations. The article also specifies measurement boundaries, disconfirming observations, and a staged research agenda. Its contribution is a conditional account of how work attitudes may influence task, contextual, and other role contributions without treating commitment as sufficient for performance or additional effort as inherently beneficial. The model remains untested. Its value depends on whether the proposed mechanisms can be distinguished empirically and explain behavior beyond established constructs such as meaningful work, perceived support, and engagement.

items.title: Large Language Models for African Languages: Systematic Review of Adaptation Strategies, Evaluation Challenges, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Large language models have transformed the landscape of natural language processing, but their practical impact fades rapidly at the edges of under-resourced languages. Many linguistic communities lack the substantial digital footprint needed to effectively leverage standard foundation models. In this paper, we present a systematic review of recent adaptation literature to explore the strategies by which under-resourced languages can benefit from pretrained architectures, avoiding the need to train from zero. With a PRISMA-guided protocol, this study tracks multilingual backbones, localized LLMs, engineering practice, and evaluation metrics. The field’s trajectory is clear: research has largely moved away from generic multilingual representation learning towards language-specific fine-tuning, instruction alignment, parameter-efficient adaptations, vocabulary adaptation, and cross-lingual transfers. However, progress is uneven, with scarce data, poorly tuned benchmarks, and inconsistent access to computational resource challenging downstream usefulness. As demonstrated by our synthesis, architecture updates alone are insufficient; instead, technical adaptation and local resource cultivation must be seen as a single community-anchored ecosystem.

items.title: Lived Experiences of Long-Term Male Sikad Drivers in Ozamiz City: A Phenomenological Study
items.abstract: Sikad drivers provide short-distance, pedal-powered transport in many Philippine communities, yet their working lives remain underrepresented in qualitative scholarship. This phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of ten long-term male sikad drivers in Ozamiz City, Misamis Occidental, Philippines. Participants were purposively selected from drivers who were married, had at least two children, and had more than 15 years of experience. In-depth interviews examined sources of motivation, everyday hardships, coping practices, and hopes for the future. The accounts were synthesised into four overarching themes: (1) family as the central source of purpose and dignity; (2) poverty, restricted opportunity, and social vulnerability; (3) faith and everyday coping; and (4) hope, perseverance, and resourcefulness. Participants described unstable earnings, difficulty meeting food and health needs, limited alternatives to informal work, road-safety concerns, competition from motorised transport, housing insecurity, and experiences of disrespect. At the same time, they emphasised responsibility to family, children's education, honesty, religious faith, gratitude, and persistent effort. The findings show that resilience among these drivers is relational and practical rather than simply individual: it is sustained by family obligations, spiritual meaning, everyday routines, and adaptive livelihood strategies while remaining constrained by informal employment and material insecurity. Because the sample was small, homogeneous, and context-specific, the findings are not intended to serve as population estimates. They nevertheless provide locally grounded evidence that can inform more inclusive discussions of informal transport, occupational health, road safety, social protection, and livelihood support.

items.title: LLM measurements that agree with human coders overall can still distort specific effects
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly adopted in the social sciences as surrogates for human coders. Standard practice validates them by their correspondence with human measurements of the same stimuli using statistics like correlation. However, overall correspondence can conceal biases that distort specific claims. We demonstrate this with open-weight LLM ratings of 568 food and 1,811 scene photographs. Ratings inflate, attenuate, or reverse effects, and improving overall correspondence with prompts can improve one contrast while worsening another. Rankings also elevate some categories and demote others beyond what random errors of the same size typically produce. Across six prompts, some of these errors are shared, so sampling across prompts may continue to mask biases. We propose validating LLM coders against specific claims they will test rather than the general coding task.

items.title: Material uncertainty in computational workflow in the archives: Holocaust last writings beyond machine-readable extraction
items.abstract: Abstract This article examines how computational archival workflows transform fragile Holocaust last writings into machine-readable data, and what is lost in that transformation. It introduces the concept of material uncertainty: the condition of textual objects whose meaning cannot be separated from the damaged, improvised, or unstable material forms through which they survive. Drawing on Holocaust literary criticism, archival theory, material trauma studies, and debates over computation in cultural heritage, the article reconstructs a typical archival workflow, from image preprocessing, segmentation, and text recognition to post-processing, translation, metadata generation, and classification. It then executes this workflow on three Holocaust last-writing limit cases: Eva Schulzová’s illustrated poem “One Night in Terezín,” Eliezer Heiman’s inscribed clay tablets, and Sal Bramson’s cloth fragment. The workflow traces show that computational tools can enhance visibility, recover words, support translation, and create access, but also risk detaching textual content from the material conditions that make these objects evidentiary. Schulzová’s poem is reorganized as recoverable verbal text while its relation among image, line, and child authorship is flattened; Heiman’s clay resists extraction because depth, soot, and flaking occupy the same visual field; Bramson’s cloth shows how partial computational success may obscure relations among drawing, caption, textile, address, and clandestine transmission. The article argues that responsible workflows must be relation-preserving rather than extraction-driven, keeping uncertainty visible rather than resolving it into cleaner data.

items.title: Mental Health Literacy Across Psychology Students and Large Language Models
items.abstract: Mental health misconceptions are widespread, yet it remains unclear how accurately psychology students distinguish such misconceptions from evidence-based information, whether this differs across stages of psychology education, and how their performance compares with that of large language models (LLMs). We evaluated the accuracy of 150 psychology students, including 70 first-semester and 80 more advanced students, in classifying 15 mental health myths and 15 facts. Additionally, we used Chat GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.5, DeepSeek V3.2, and GLM-5 to classify the same statements across 80 independent runs per statement and model. Students classified mental health myths more accurately than facts, and advanced students outperformed first-semester students in classifying both statement types (myths: 87.7% vs. 75.2%; facts: 69.3% vs. 55.4%). A binomial generalized linear mixed-effects model indicated that group differences in classification accuracy varied between myths and facts. LLMs generally showed higher accuracy than both student groups in classifying statements, although performance varied substantially across models, particularly for facts. Item-level analyses revealed partly distinct error patterns: students and LLMs struggled with some of the same facts, whereas they also showed relative advantages on specific statements. These findings suggest that mental health literacy differs significantly across stages of psychology education and that, although current LLMs perform strongly on this classification task, some item-specific errors recurred across repeated runs. Examining which misconceptions and facts remain difficult may help identify specific gaps in both psychology education and AI-generated mental health information.

items.title: Modeling the Effect of Prolonged Wakefulness on Human Performance Using a Dual-Process QN-MHP-U
items.abstract: Accurately predicting human performance during prolonged wakefulness is essential for safety in high-risk environments, where operators are often required to maintain wakefulness over extended periods without sleep. The present study integrates the circadian process (Process C) and the sleep homeostatic process (Process S) into the Queuing Network-Model Human Processor-Unified (QN-MHP-U) via Server 9 to predict human performance during prolonged wakefulness. The model is applied to a system monitoring task, where operators must monitor analog gauges and warning lights and respond promptly to abnormal signals—a task type that is both representative of real-world monitoring duties and highly vulnerable to arousal decline. The model predicts reaction time on this task over 25 hr of wakefulness, achieving an RMSE of 0.41. The developed computational model can be further applied to domains requiring long-duration work, such as aviation and nuclear power operations.

items.title: Motion Capture of Bronchoscopist Kinematics Using a Spatial Computing Device: A Methodological Proof-of-Concept Study.
items.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Bronchoscopy is physically demanding, and studies of ergonomics and objective skill assessment require accurate, segment-resolved capture of the bronchoscopist's hand and head movements. However, existing motion capture approaches typically rely on specialized laboratory infrastructure or wearable sensor arrays, limiting their routine use. METHODS: A board-certified pulmonologist performed 10 systematic bronchoscopies across the 18 named segments using an airway simulator and a single-use bronchoscope. Procedures alternated between conditions without and with engagement of the bronchoscope's insertion-tube rotation mechanism. A custom visionOS application running on Apple Vision Pro captured bilateral hand and head poses at 30 Hz, with synchronized voice-cue annotations for each segment. RESULTS: All 180 expected segment insertions were recorded (94.4% via voice cues; 5.6% recovered through tracking-derived hold detection and excluded from per-insertion analyses). Intermittent tracking-freezing artifacts, in which a static pose was retained under a valid tracking flag, were detected by frame-to-frame immobility and excluded from the affected analyses. The mean per-insertion peak left-wrist rotation across all segments was 107.9° without and 72.6° with the rotation mechanism. The mean left-thumb path length within the wrist's local reference frame was 3.82 ± 0.48 m per bronchoscopy, and the estimated number of bronchoscope lever operation cycles was 64.8 ± 7.9 per procedure. CONCLUSION: In this proof-of-concept study, a single off-the-shelf head-mounted device enabled multi-channel capture of bronchoscopist kinematics during simulated bronchoscopy. This approach provides a practical methodological foundation for future studies on bronchoscopy ergonomics, skill assessment, and AI-driven training data generation.

items.title: Natural Disasters and Emergency Preparedness
items.abstract: Natural and technological disasters pose significant threats to public health, and their frequency and severity are intensifying under the influence of climate change. This chapter examines the full spectrum of disaster types, including hurricanes, floods, tsunamis, droughts, and technological events such as oil spills and train derailments, and explores their public health consequences across mortality, mental health, communicable disease, maternal and child health, occupational health, and environmental health services. The disaster management cycle, encompassing preparedness, response, mitigation, and recovery, is presented as a policy framework, with attention to the governance architecture that guides action at federal, state, and local levels. Key legislation, including the Stafford Act, PAHPA, and major environmental statutes, is reviewed alongside case studies of Hurricane Katrina, the Deepwater Horizon oil spill, and repeated disaster events to illustrate real-world policy successes and failures. The chapter highlights community resilience as both a policy goal and a measurable capacity and addresses emerging challenges, including aging infrastructure and data-sharing barriers. Practical tools for public health decision-makers and opportunities offered by AI-enhanced surveillance and remote sensing are also discussed.

items.title: No universal patient: temporal logics of harm prevention in emotional AI healthcare across Japan, China, and Hong Kong
items.abstract: Abstract Across East Asia, emotional AI in healthcare is governed through markedly different normative and institutional rationalities that construct the patient, harm, and vulnerability in distinct ways. This article develops a triadic analytical framework, integrating moral anthropologies, models of legitimacy, and regulatory instruments, to examine governance rationalities in Japan, China, and Hong Kong. Instead of treating Asian perspectives as variations on Euro-American principlism, this analysis examines these jurisdictions in their own right, showing how each constructs the patient differently, as relational node, protected subject, or rights-holder, and prioritises different harms accordingly. Using PARO, a therapeutic companion robot deployed globally in elderly care, as a stylised analytical device, the article shows that the same robot becomes three different regulatory objects. This case study surfaces a fourth dimension of governance rationality: temporal orientation. Japan’s governance rationality is iterative, allowing norms to emerge through use and professional dialogue; China’s is preventive, anticipating and regulating harms before deployment; and Hong Kong’s is reactive, adjudicating violations after they occur. These temporal orientations shape harm-prevention outcomes as consequentially as the choice of instruments, and constitute the article’s primary empirical contribution. Extending Cheong’s analysis of structural accountability gaps and Zuboff’s account of how institutional power determines which technological harms become actionable, the comparison suggests that vulnerability, harm, and accountability function as governance-produced categories rather than as properties inherent to the technology. The article argues that governing emotional AI requires not harmonisation of principles but recognition of ontological difference, an epistemological reorientation with direct implications for transnational governance frameworks.

items.title: Occupation-specific Physiotherapy and Ergonomic Rehabilitation in Seronegative Radiographic Axial Spondyloarthritis in a Young Farm Labourer: A Case Report
items.abstract: Axial Spondyloarthritis (axial SpA) is often missed in young people, often confused with mechanical Low Back Pain (LBP), especially among those with heavy manual labour, resulting in poor management and loss of function. This case report details a 22-year-old male farm labourer who had suffered from chronic LBP (4/10 with activity and 7/10 at rest) for 1.5 years, progressive stiffness in the spine (morning stiffness> 60 minutes), and decreased work capacity. On clinical examination, decreased lumbar mobility (flexion 40°), decreased chest expansion (2.5 cm), posterior chain muscle tightness, and guarded movement without neurological deficit were noted. Laboratory investigations revealed an elevated ESR (42 mm/hour), a borderline normal C-Reactive Protein (CRP: 4.2 mg/L; reference <5 mg/L), which, while within the normal range, may carry diagnostic relevance in axial SpA, and negative HLA-B27 and rheumatoid factor. Unilateral grade II sacroiliitis (modified NY criteria) and vertebral squaring with early syndesmophytes were seen on radiographs, compatible with seronegative radiographic axial SpA. The patient fulfilled the Assessment of SpondyloArthritis International Society (ASAS) criteria for radiographic axial SpA (sacroiliitis on imaging plus ≥1 SpA feature). Amor classification criteria confirmed the diagnosis at the minimum threshold (score 6, threshold ≥6); notably, the radiological sacroiliitis item scored 0 points as unilateral grade II sacroiliitis does not meet the Amor radiological criterion (which requires bilateral ≥ Grade II or unilateral ≥ Grade III), and the total of 6 points was reached through clinical features alone. Baseline assessment indicated high disease activity and functional limitation {Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI) 5.6; Functional Index (BASFI): 5.3; Metrology Index (BASMI): 2.4; Global Score (BAS-G): 8.5}. A structured 12-week physiotherapy program including spinal mobility and extension exercises, flexibility training, breathing exercises and postural correction was implemented, along with occupationspecific ergonomic interventions including neutral spine lifting, load redistribution (≤15 kg), work modification, and use of longhandled tools. At 12-week follow-up, clinically meaningful improvements were observed: BASDAI score was 3.4, BASFI score was 3.1, BASMI score was 1.6, BAS-G score was 4.2, pain score 3/10 during activity and 5/10 at rest, and a 34% improvement in work productivity (Work Productivity and Activity Impairment (WPAI) questionnaire). Improvements in BASDAI and BASFI exceeded established Minimal Clinically Important Difference (MCID) thresholds. This case emphasises early recognition of inflammatory back pain. It highlights the role of physiotherapy combined with occupation-specific ergonomic modifications in improving function and work participation among manual workers with seronegative axial SpA.

items.title: Occupational Contact Dermatitis in Italy: Bridging the Gap Between Estimated Incidence and Official Reporting Data
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Occupational Contact Dermatitis (OCD) is one of the most common occupational diseases and represents a substantial clinical and socioeconomic burden. Despite its high prevalence, OCD is frequently underrecognised and underreported, limiting the effectiveness of occupational health surveillance and preventive strategies. This study aimed to investigate the extent of OCD underreporting in Italy by comparing official reporting data with incidence estimates derived from epidemiological data available in the scientific literature. Methods: Official data on dermatitis and eczema cases reported to the Italian National Institute for Insurance against Accidents at Work (INAIL) between 2020 and 2024 were analysed and compared with incidence estimates obtained through a systematic literature search of epidemiological studies, surveillance systems, and cohort studies conducted in high-risk occupational groups with available specific incidence data in the scientific literature, such as healthcare workers, construction workers, and hairdressers. Results: INAIL data showed an average of approximately 182 reported OCD cases per year during the study period. However, the estimates we calculated suggested a substantially higher disease burden, with an annual estimate ranging from 1439 cases to 21,412 cases. This implies that, depending on the incidence source used, only 0.8% to 12.7% of the expected cases are notified. Conclusions: OCD appears to be substantially underreported in Italy. Underrecognition of its occupational origin, the low severity often attributed to symptoms, and the limits of current surveillance systems likely contribute. Better occupational health surveillance, greater awareness among clinicians and workers, and simpler reporting procedures would improve case recognition and help prevent progression to chronic disease.

items.title: Occupational disparities in chronic disease prevalence and metabolic covariation: a cross-sectional study of six occupational groups in Lanzhou
items.abstract: Objectives To investigate the differences in chronic disease prevalence and underlying metabolic profiles among working-age individuals across six typical occupational groups, identify occupation-related associated factors, and provide epidemiological evidence for occupation-specific precise prevention and control of chronic diseases. Methods A cross-sectional study design was adopted. A total of 1,473 on-the-job physical examinees aged 18–64 who received physical examination at the Physical Examination Center of the First Hospital of Lanzhou University from August 2024 to August 2025 were retrospectively included. Structured questionnaires were distributed via targeted online channels to collect sociodemographic characteristics and behavioral and lifestyle data. Physical examinations and laboratory tests were performed to obtain 16 health indicators. Age-standardized prevalence (ASR) of five chronic diseases (hypertension, diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, hyperuricemia, and obesity) was calculated using the direct standardization method, with the age composition of the full study sample as the standard population. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was conducted to assess the independent associations between various factors and chronic diseases, and Spearman rank correlation analysis was used to evaluate the strength of associations between health indicators. Results Occupational disparities in the prevalence of hyperlipidemia and hyperuricemia were the most prominent. After age standardization, the prevalence of hyperlipidemia in police officers (ASR = 0.435, 95% CI 0.368–0.502) and software engineers (ASR = 0.418, 95% CI 0.366–0.470), as well as the prevalence of hyperuricemia in firefighters (ASR = 0.381, 95% CI 0.315–0.447) and police officers (ASR = 0.332, 95% CI 0.267–0.396) were all significantly higher than those in healthcare workers (ASR = 0.218 for hyperlipidemia and 0.143 for hyperuricemia, respectively), with no overlap in 95% CIs across occupational groups. Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that police officers (OR = 2.499, 95% CI 1.409–4.433) and software engineers (OR = 2.531, 95% CI 1.007–6.361) were independent associated factors for hyperlipidemia; police officers (OR = 3.425, 95% CI 1.821–6.441), firefighters (OR = 4.143, 95% CI 1.916–8.955), and software engineers (OR = 2.957, 95% CI 1.136–7.696) were independent associated factors for hyperuricemia. No statistically significant occupational disparities were observed for hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and obesity. Correlation analysis showed that triglyceride, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, body mass index, uric acid and alanine aminotransferase formed a moderate correlation cluster (| r | = 0.44–0.54), body mass index was widely correlated with a variety of metabolic indicators ( r = 0.39–0.51), and uric acid was strongly correlated with creatinine ( r = 0.64). Conclusion Police officers, firefighters, and software engineers are occupational groups with elevated prevalence of hyperlipidemia and hyperuricemia. Age standardization is a necessary methodological step for cross-occupational health comparisons. Obesity occupies a core hub position in the metabolic comorbidity network. These findings provide reference evidence for developing occupation-specific, tiered precise prevention and control strategies for chronic diseases.

items.title: Occupational Injuries and Illnesses Under the Employment Permit System: Exploring Perceptions and Responses of Migrant Workers in South Korea
items.abstract: The number of migrant workers for temporary labor has rapidly increased, alongside high mortality rates in South Korea. This study explores the occupational safety and health conditions of migrant workers employed under the Employment Permit System (EPS). Data were collected through in-depth interviews with 11 EPS migrant workers who had experienced occupational injuries and illnesses, supplemented by secondary data such as official government guidelines, administrative manuals, and relevant legislation. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis. The results are as follows: first, regarding migrant workers' perceptions of the workplace environments that contributed to occupational injuries and illnesses, four subthemes were identified: restricted access to EPS workplace information; assignment to small-scale workplaces; inadequate safety training; and nominally conducted safety inspections. Second, three subthemes emerged regarding the contexts that prevented migrant workers from appropriately responding to their occupational injuries and illnesses: inaccessibility of medical services; institutional barriers to the Workers' Compensation System; and lack of the right to transfer workplaces. Based on the results, this study highlights the importance of linking occupational health and safety policy with labor migration policy.

items.title: Older adults do not have a higher metabolic cost than younger adults in outdoor overground walking
items.abstract: The metabolic cost of walking is widely used to evaluate human performance and effectiveness of clinical interventions. Decades of laboratory research, largely based on treadmill experiments, have established a canonical relationship between walking speed and metabolic cost, and suggested that ageing shifts this relationship upward, implying reduced efficiency in older adults. However, this relationship has not been well tested during overground walking across matched speeds. We compared healthy younger (n=16; 26±2yr) and older (n=11; 74±3yr) adults across eight outdoor overground walking trials at different speeds: preferred walking speed (PWS), three fixed speeds (0.8, 1.2, 1.6 m·s⁻¹), and four speeds at ±5% and ±10% of PWS. Contrary to our hypothesis, older adults did not show higher gross or net metabolic cost of walking (GCOW and NCOW) than younger adults at any speed; rather, both trended consistently lower in older adults, reaching significance for GCOW at 0.8 m·s⁻¹ only. Comparisons of resting metabolic rate and respiratory exchange ratio to prior reference groups did not indicate that our older cohort was unusually fit. Independent of age, GCOW was significantly higher at 0.8 m·s⁻¹ than at the remaining speeds (1.2-1.6 m·s⁻¹), confirming that walking at slower speeds increases GCOW. These findings challenge the view that ageing intrinsically increases the energetic cost of walking, suggesting instead that previously reported upward shifts in cost may reflect treadmill-specific constraints or speed effects. Future work is needed to explore direct comparisons of outdoor, overground walking with treadmill walking at fixed speeds in both younger and older adults.

items.title: One Health
items.abstract: One Health is an integrative framework that recognizes the functional interdependence of human, animal, plant, and ecosystem health. This chapter examines the concept&s;s historical evolution; its policy landscape at the city, state, national, and international levels; and the ongoing gaps that limit effective implementation. Beginning with foundational definitions and the drivers of One Health relevance, including zoonotic disease emergence, climate change, land-use change, antimicrobial resistance, and biodiversity loss, the chapter surveys U.S. policies across human health, animal health, plant health, and ecosystem protection. Case studies on H5N1 in dairy cattle and poultry and COVID-19 wastewater surveillance illustrate both progress and shortcomings in cross-sector coordination. Occupational health risks at the human–animal interface are also addressed. Key policy gaps identified include siloed data systems, uneven investment in One Health workforce development, lagging environmental surveillance, and disparities between high-income countries and low- and middle-income countries. The chapter concludes by highlighting emerging opportunities, including regional consortia and national academy initiatives, to accelerate intersectoral collaboration and build a more resilient One Health policy framework.

items.title: Partitioning menus to nudge single-item choice
items.abstract: Decision makers are often called on to choose a single item from a menu of options: employees pick health plans from provider-sponsored lists, citizens vote for a representative among candidates, physicians select a treatment from an order set. Because options are often organized or grouped into subsets, the question arises whether the grouping of menu items affects the options ultimately selected by decision makers. Across ten experiments, we provide robust evidence of single-item partition dependence — decision makers are more likely to choose from response categories that are more finely partitioned, holding the underlying set of options constant. For example, an employee choosing a health plan from a menu that lists HMOs individually but groups PPOs into a single category with sub-options may be biased toward choosing an HMO. Unlike prior work on multi-item allocation decisions, the traditional explanation of partition dependence — a bias toward even allocation — cannot apply to single-item choice, because singular choices are not divisible. Instead, we find that finer partitions receive greater choice share because decision makers infer that separately listed options are more popular on average than grouped ones. More broadly, strategic partitioning of the menu space may serve as a simple and effective tool for managers, policymakers, and choice architects: listing options separately rather than grouping them together tends to increase their choice share, without fundamentally altering the underlying set of alternatives or the effort required to choose among them.

items.title: Peer mentoring for newly arrived migrant pupils
items.abstract: Abstract European classrooms have become increasingly diverse, raising questions for schools about how to support newly arrived migrant (NAM) pupils as they navigate academic and social transitions. This paper is an explorative, qualitative study of peer mentoring programmes for NAM pupils in the Netherlands, Spain, and Ireland and presents a comparison of the countries’ mentoring program systems. It focuses on recognition, design, and perceived outcomes of these programmes. Despite the small number of surveyed teachers ( n = 47) and pupils ( n = 43) and an uneven distribution of teachers between the countries, a conclusion can be that peer mentoring is not widely recognised or implemented, partly due to a narrow conceptualization or misrecognition of peer mentoring. Among schools that implement mentoring, programmes vary in design but share a focus on social connection and academic support. They mostly rely on voluntary participation and intrinsic motivation and have little structure, training, compensation, and feedback. Teachers generally report positive perceived outcomes, while pupil responses showed strong individual variation. No consistent differences emerged between countries or education systems.

items.abstract: Conventional Pancasila and Citizenship Education often remains teacher-centered, potentially contributing to cognitive fatigue and academic anxiety while limiting students’ meaningful engagement with learning. This study examines the implementation of the Deep Learning approach through three interconnected pillars—Mindful, Meaningful, and Joyful Learning—and explores its influence on students’ learning behaviors and psychological responses. Using a descriptive qualitative design, the study involved one fifth-grade teacher and nine fifth-grade students at State Elementary School 060814 Medan as key informants. Data were collected across four classroom meetings through participatory observation using teacher-behavior and student-learning-behavior indicators, complemented by in-depth interviews. The findings revealed a consistent improvement in the teacher’s implementation of the three pillars, including more effective reflective activities through Sharing Circles. Students demonstrated a shift from surface-level memorization toward deeper information processing and contextual understanding. Interview findings further indicated reduced academic anxiety, increased confidence and self-efficacy, and stronger intrinsic motivation. These findings suggest that Deep Learning can foster a more reflective, meaningful, and psychologically supportive environment for Pancasila and Citizenship Education.

items.title: Pharmacological human augmentation, fatigue management and spatial disorientation training during distant air operations: lessons learned from the wars in Iran
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Military aviation in distant operations increases aircrew fatigue and the risk of human-factor-related safety incidents. This study evaluated the impact of different fatigue management and pharmacological human augmentation approaches on flight safety and, in a separate analysis, the effect of prior spatial disorientation (SD) simulator training on in-flight SD severity. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed human-factor-related safety incidents in the Israeli Air Force across three operational periods: Operation 'Iron Swords' (short-range, lower-tempo), 'Rising Lion' (12-day long-range, high-tempo) and 'Epic Fury' (42-day extended-duration, high-tempo). The primary outcome was the normalised rate of safety incidents per flight hour. Secondary outcomes included the normalised utilisation of caffeine and modafinil and the severity of SD events among trained versus untrained aircrew. RESULTS: Across the three periods, 949 incidents were reported. Normalised incident rates and severity distributions remained stable between 'Rising Lion' and 'Epic Fury', despite the latter's significantly greater flight volume. The fighter fleet, the only platform to fully implement preplanned, individualised flight-and-rest scheduling and personalised stimulant prescriptions, was also the only platform to demonstrate a decrease in normalised incident rates (r=-0.82, p=0.004). Aircrew who had never undergone SD simulator training sustained significantly more severe SD events than previously trained aircrew (p=0.015). CONCLUSIONS: Implementing individualised physiological envelopes-combining personalised pharmacological augmentation with structured rest-was associated with stable or reduced in-flight safety incident rates during sustained, high-tempo operations. Additionally, prior SD simulator training was associated with a decreased level of severity of SD events.

items.title: Play Through Children’s Eyes—The Subjective Meaning of Play to Young Children
items.abstract: Abstract Play is fundamental to children’s daily activities and provides a critical avenue for learning and development. However, attempts to describe and operationalize play are dominated by adults’ perspectives. This study aims to explore the subjective meaning of play to young children. Using a qualitative approach, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 327 children aged 4 to 8 years from [a Western European country]. These interviews were analyzed using both deductive and inductive content analysis methods to categorize children’s descriptions of play. Approximately half of the children provided coherent, differentiated descriptions of play. Results indicate that children’s perceptions align deductively with the features of play seminally defined by Krasnor and Pepler (1980) and expanded by Smith and Vollstedt (1985): positive affect, flexibility, intrinsic motivation, nonliterality, and means before end. The inductive analysis identified three additional categories, children’s business, social interactions, and object reference and therefore revealed additional features of play relevant for children. This study underscores the importance of recognizing children’s voices in research and highlights the complex, multifaceted nature of play from a child’s perspective. These insights into children’s perspectives contribute to a deeper understanding of play and inform educators, parents, and policymakers about the elements to play in early childhood. Future research should continue to explore the nuanced views of children to better support their developmental needs through play.

items.title: Pro-Active Approach in the Context of Quality 5.0 Challenges
items.abstract: This study examines entrepreneurs’ awareness and preventive activities regarding the environment and employees as key elements of the Quality 5.0 concept. Quantitative research was conducted among 380 manufacturing companies in Greater Poland that had not implemented or certified a quality management system. Data were collected using CATI interviews using an original questionnaire assessing the importance and implementation of 24 preventive management factors, with a detailed analysis of 10 factors. The findings identify maintaining good relations with the environment (K2), careful supplier selection and continuous evaluation (K3), improving employee qualifications and skills (K7), and ensuring occupational safety and ergonomics (K8) as the most important preventive management factors. The combined IPA and paired analyses identify K7—improving employee qualifications and skills—as the clearest improvement priority: it was the only factor in the “concentrate here” quadrant, had the largest importance–implementation gap (0.34), and the largest rank-biserial effect (rrb = 0.639). K2—maintaining good relations with the environment—and K8—ensuring occupational safety and ergonomics—combined high importance with high implementation and should therefore be maintained, while K5—selection of employees based on their competencies—also warrants attention due to its gap of 0.28. Paired Wilcoxon tests showed statistically significant implementation shortfalls for all ten factors after Holm correction, indicating that the gap between perceived importance and implementation is systematic. Participatory management (K6) received the lowest importance and implementation ratings, although its large paired effect suggests that its relatively low IPA priority should not be interpreted as evidence of low relevance. Associations with company size and years in operation were generally weak and factor-specific. The results contribute to understanding preventive management as a basis for sustainable, human-centered, and proactive Quality 5.0 practices. They suggest that managerial priorities should consider both the relative IPA position and the magnitude of importance–implementation gaps, with particular attention to employee competence development and participatory management. The results emphasize the role of preventive management practices in supporting the Quality 5.0 concept and provide practical guidance for organizations seeking to strengthen sustainable, employee-oriented, and proactive management approaches.

items.title: Protean Career Orientation and Flow: A Conceptual Perspective on Employee Retention in the Hospitality Industry
items.abstract: The changing nature of the modern workplace requires that employees take greater responsibility for managing their own careers. With the hospitality sector being the industries with high turnover, understanding the factors that influence employee retention has become important. This paper aims to provide a conceptual framework for examining the relationship between protean career orientation and the intention to quit, with flow proposed as a psychological mediator. This study integrates Protean Career Theory and Flow Theory, proposing that flow mediates how self-driven and values-driven protean career orientations influence the intention to quit. Protean individuals are suggested to be less likely to leave their organizations because their intrinsic motivation, deep absorption, and meaningful work engagement lead them to experience flow. This study provides theoretical, empirical, conceptual and practical contributions through the proposed framework. The findings suggest that employee motivation and retention can be sustained through creating work environments that foster autonomy and personal growth.

items.title: Quantitatively exploring the dark ride experience model
items.abstract: Dark rides are popular, archetypal theme park attractions, yet empirical research on their visitor experience remains limited. This study provides a quantitative exploration of Cornelis and Strijbosch's (2024) dark ride experience model, which describes how immersion, emotions, cognitions, and attentional switching (driven by switch factors of motivation, opportunity and ability) shape overall evaluations. Using self-report data from 770 visitors across nine dark rides at a Western European theme park, collected with a purpose-built post-experience survey, we tested 15 derived hypotheses. Results offer partial, context-bound support: switch factors, immersion, and positive emotions consistently predicted overall evaluations both directly and indirectly, whereas findings on cognitive engagement and negative emotions remain inconclusive. Implications for future dark ride research, design and development are discussed.

items.title: Readiness for Implementing Activity-Based Costing in Determining Production Costs and Cost Efficiency among Food Processing MSMEs in Bekasi City
items.abstract: This study aims to analyze the application of Activity-Based Costing (ABC) in determining the cost of production (HPP) for food-processing MSMEs in Bekasi City. MSMEs play an important role in Indonesia’s economy but still face challenges in achieving accurate HPP due to conventional costing methods that often produce cost distortions. ABC is chosen because it allocates costs based on actual activities consuming resources, thus providing more accurate and relevant cost information. This research employs a contextual qualitative approach by exploring the experiences of MSME actors in implementing ABC, including human factors, work culture, and resource limitations. The focus is not only on HPP accuracy but also on the impact of ABC on cost efficiency and pricing strategies. The findings are expected to show that ABC enhances MSME competitiveness through more realistic cost calculations, control of non-value-added activities, and competitive pricing. The novelty of this study lies in developing a conceptual ABC model relevant to Indonesian MSMEs, as well as integrating simple digital accounting technology to support sustainable implementation. Therefore, this research contributes to strengthening MSME cost systems and provides a basis for policies and managerial accounting training in the small business sector.

items.title: Recommendations for the use of topographic field aerial survey systems for updating large-scale topographic plans
items.abstract: Background. The article examines the current problem of rapid updating of topographic plans at a scale of 1 : 500 in conditions of an urgent need for rapid updating of geospatial data for the needs of engineering and cadastre. The use of traditional methods of ground surveying often turns out to be ineffective due to high labor intensity. The integration of modern unmanned systems into the workflow ensures the generation of detailed orthophoto maps with ultra-high resolution. The purpose of the study is to substantiate and develop practical recommendations for the use of modern topographic field aerial survey complexes for updating large-scale terrain plans. Methods. Modern topographic complexes DJI Inspire 2 and specialized P316 systems were used to conduct the study. The research methodology is based on a complex combination of advanced photogrammetric processing of image data in the Pix4Dmatic environment and subsequent vectorization of objects in ArcGIS Pro. Special attention is paid to the use of high-precision positioning technologies Real Time Kinematic and Post-Processed Kinematic for determining coordinates of the ground control points (GCPs). This approach makes it possible to ensure strict adherence to geometric parameters when building digital terrain models and to automate the process of creating a topographic database. Results. During the study, optimal technical parameters of aerial photography and digital data processing algorithms were established, allowing to stably achieve the root mean square error of the position of objects within 0.05 m. The study demonstrates the significant advantages of modern specialized software in substantially increasing the overall productivity of surveying professionals. It is experimentally proven that the use of the Pix4Dmatic and ArcGIS Pro combination allows to significantly reduce the time for office-based processing, while ensuring a high level of detail and accuracy required for 1 : 500 scale plans. Conclusions. A comprehensive technological scheme for updating plans has been proposed and tested, which ensures high accuracy of the results obtained and significantly reduces the time for performing office work due to a high degree of automation of the main processes. The implementation of the methodology based on modern topographic field aerial survey systems allows minimizing the impact of the human factor and optimizing resource requirements when creating large-scale cartographic products. The practical application of the developed recommendations confirmed their effectiveness for operational territory monitoring, which is critically important for updating geospatial databases in modern conditions.
